Synopsis:
Florrick's dialog when you helped her leave the fortress.

Cluster Contexts:
- WYR_WyrmRockPrison_FlorrickOutisdeFortress.json: The player has just freed Councillor Florrick from a cell in Wyrm Rock Prison and is escorting her out; she thanks the party for rescuing her and for bolstering her courage. Off‑screen choices determine how that escape plays out — you may have cleared guards and Flaming Fist forces by force, slipped out via a janitor’s tunnel, or seen guard presence altered by prior confrontations (for example with Gortash or events in the Steel Watch/Foundry). Florrick alternates between despair and being rallyable: if persuaded she vows to use her political connections to help you later, but freeing her also sends her straight back into the fight for the city. Outcomes from related scenes (Orin/Netherstone results, the Foundry/Neurocitor, and dealings with Gortash) can change how effective her aid will be.
- WYR_WyrmRockPrison_Florrick.json: You are talking to Councillor Florrick, who is locked in a cell in Wyrm Rock Prison and can be freed — the cell key is carried by one of the guards. After you unlock her she will ask you to escort her out; you can make that escape by either killing all the guards in the prison, the Flaming Fist office, and one bridge, or by finding a secret tunnel in the janitor’s closet. Florrick alternates between despair (Ravengard and the city are lost) and being rallyable — if convinced she promises to use her connections to aid you once free. Off‑screen actions (for example confronting Lord Gortash in his office or events in the Steel Watch/Foundry) may already have changed guard presence, Flaming Fist attitudes, or other conditions that affect the escape and outcomes.
- IRN_IronThrone_Return.json: Outcome dialog for the Iron throne. Major part with Ravengard thanking the player, explaining that the emperor extended their protection to Ravengard, and that Ravengard will wait for them in camp where they can talk again.
- HAV_Florrick.json: Florrick is with her Flaming Fist troops in Haven. As you approach, they are furiously trying to put a plan together to rescue Ravengard. The curse is one thing, but Ketheric is invincible. They can't just storm the place. And even if they could, they would execute the prisoners if the alarm was raised - including the Grand Duke.Florrick turns to you, incredibly grateful that we have made it so far. She implores you to work with Jaheira for her rescue efforts, but tells you your priority is clear: Duke Ravengard. He must be returned to the city - it will not survive his absence.
- LOW_MurderTribunal_Valeria.json: Interactive dialogue with Valeria after taking down the Murder Tribunal and saving her from the Baptism of Blood. She will head off after this and disappear out of sight.

Dialogue Excerpts (up to 3 samples, ordered):

- Counsellor Florrick: This is far enough - the way should be clear. (node 20)
- Counsellor Florrick: I can't thank you enough. For getting me out of that damned prison. And for giving me courage when I'd all but run out. (node 4)
- Jaheira: Don't be so quick with your gratitude, Counsellor. All we have done is send you back into the battle. || [context] NodeContext: Wryly amused - yes, we saved an ally, but she's going to need to work for it now. She might wish we'd left her where she was. (node 22)

- Wyll: It's the least we could do. Your faith in this city should inspire us all. (node 11)

context: You have just freed Councillor Florrick from a cell in Wyrm Rock Prison and are escorting her out; she thanks the party for rescuing her and for bolstering her courage, and notes the route is clear. Off‑screen choices (for example whether you cleared guards and Flaming Fist forces by force, slipped out through a janitor’s tunnel, or already confronted Gortash or events in the Foundry/Steel Watch) determine how that escape played out. Florrick shifts between despair and being rallyable — in this moment she’s grateful and resolute, but can also be pushed back into hopelessness; if convinced she vows to use her political connections to help later. Companions’ lines (Jaheira’s warning, Wyll’s encouragement) reflect the tension that freeing her sends her straight back into the fight for the city, and outcomes from other scenes will affect how much help she can actually provide.
